lines.rookie:
Detective,
Last night the lamps did not go out on their own.
One of the two strangers came into the lamp house.
He did not touch the fire. He did not touch the coal.
He took off the long leather belt that turns the big wheel.
I put it back at dawn. His muddy hand is still on it.
lines.junior:
Detective,
The lamps did not go out by themselves last night.
One of the two strangers slipped into the lamp house.
He did not touch the fire. He did not touch the coal either.
He took off the long leather belt that turns the big wheel.
I put it back at dawn. His muddy handprint is still on it.
lines.master:
Detective,
Last night's darkness was no accident of the lamps.
One of the two strangers crept into the lamp house.
He did not touch the fire. He did not touch the coal.
He took off the long leather belt that drives the big wheel.
I fitted it back at dawn. The print of his muddy hand remains on it.

lines.rookie: In the dark, the strangers walked from the east gate to the Queen's hall. One carried a flat board.
lines.junior: In the darkness, the strangers walked from the east gate to the Queen's hall. One of them carried a flat board.
lines.master: Under cover of dark, the strangers walked from the east gate to the Queen's hall, one carrying a flat board.

lines.rookie: You found the rope under the Queen's steps.
lines.junior: You found this rope under the Queen's steps.
lines.master: You pulled this rope from beneath the Queen's steps.

lines.rookie: One stranger dropped it as the lamps came back.
lines.junior: One of the strangers dropped it when the lamps came back on.
lines.master: One stranger must have dropped it as the lamps flickered back to life.

lines.rookie: "Builders measure with ropes like this," Lady Han says.
lines.junior: "Builders measure with ropes like this one," Lady Han says.
lines.master: "Builders take measurements with ropes like this," Lady Han tells you.

lines.rookie: Why measure a path? To draw a map of it.
lines.junior: Why would anyone measure a path? To draw a map of it.
lines.master: Why would anyone measure a path? Only to draw a map of it.

lines.rookie: You remember the man with the flat board. You look behind the steps again.
lines.junior: You remember the man with the flat board, so you look behind the steps again.
lines.master: You recall the man with the flat board and search behind the steps once more.

lines.rookie: There it is, in the leaves: a flat board with lines and dots!
lines.junior: There it is, hidden in the leaves: a flat board with lines and dots!
lines.master: There, half hidden in the leaves, lies a flat board covered in lines and dots!

lines.rookie: "The King must see this," Lady Han says.
lines.junior: "The King must see this at once," Lady Han says.
lines.master: "The King must see this at once," Lady Han insists.

lines.rookie: The King's hall
lines.junior: The King's hall
lines.master: The King's hall

lines.rookie: The lamp house
lines.junior: The lamp house
lines.master: The lamp house

lines.rookie: The Queen's hall
lines.junior: The Queen's hall
lines.master: The Queen's hall

lines.rookie: The far door has 52 steps, and no circle. How many steps to the circled door?
lines.junior: The far door is 52 steps away, and it has no circle. How many steps to the circled door?
lines.master: The far door lies 52 steps off and bears no circle. How many steps lead to the circled door?

lines.rookie: The lamp house is the square with the X and the wheel. It is not a door with a circle.
lines.junior: The lamp house is the square with the X and the wheel. It is not a door with a circle.
lines.master: The square with the X and the wheel is the lamp house, not a door with a circle.

lines.rookie: three big dots and seven small dots
lines.junior: three big dots and seven small dots
lines.master: three big dots and seven small dots

lines.rookie: a door with a circle
lines.junior: a door with a circle
lines.master: a door with a circle

lines.rookie: You bring the strangers' board to the King and the Queen.
lines.junior: You carry the strangers' board to the King and the Queen.
lines.master: You lay the strangers' board before the King and the Queen.

lines.rookie: It has no names. Only lines, dots and marks.
lines.junior: It has no names on it, only lines, dots and marks.
lines.master: Not one name is written on it: only lines, dots and marks.

lines.rookie: The Queen asks, "Whose door is marked?"
lines.junior: The Queen leans closer. "Whose door is marked?"
lines.master: The Queen leans in and asks quietly, "Whose door is marked?"

lines.rookie: The board:
lines.junior: What the board shows:
lines.master: What the strangers' board shows:

lines.rookie:
A line starts at the east gate.
It goes to a door with a circle.
By the circled door: three big dots and seven small dots.
Another line goes to a far door. By it: five big dots and two small dots. No circle.
By the pond is a square with an X. A wheel is drawn in the square.
The dots count like the knots on the rope.
lines.junior:
A line starts at the east gate.
It runs to a door with a circle.
By the circled door are three big dots and seven small dots.
Another line runs to a far door, with five big dots and two small dots by it. That door has no circle.
By the pond is a square with an X, and a wheel is drawn inside the square.
The dots count just like the knots on the rope.
lines.master:
A line begins at the east gate.
It leads to a door with a circle.
Beside the circled door sit three big dots and seven small dots.
A second line leads to a far door, marked with five big dots and two small dots but no circle.
Beside the pond is a square with an X, a wheel drawn within it.
Each dot counts like the knots on the rope: ten, or one.

lines.rookie: Whose door has the circle? Tap the picture.
lines.junior: Whose door did the strangers circle? Tap its picture.
lines.master: Whose door have the strangers marked with a circle? Tap its picture.

lines.rookie: A big dot is ten steps. A small dot is one step, like the rope.
lines.junior: A big dot means ten steps and a small dot means one step, just like the rope.
lines.master: As on the rope, a big dot stands for ten steps and a small dot for one.

lines.rookie: Your rope measured 37 steps from the east gate. To whose door?
lines.junior: Your rope measured 37 steps from the east gate. Whose door did it end at?
lines.master: Your rope measured 37 steps from the east gate. At whose door did it end?

lines.rookie: The circle is the Queen's door: 37 steps from the east gate!
lines.junior: The circle marks the Queen's door, 37 steps from the east gate!
lines.master: The circle marks the Queen's own door, 37 steps from the east gate!

lines.rookie: "And the X is the lamp house," says the King. "They will make the dark again."
lines.junior: "And the X is the lamp house," says the King. "They plan to make the dark again."
lines.master: "And the X marks the lamp house," the King says. "They mean to bring the dark again."

lines.rookie: Lady Han says, "Japan wants more power in Korea. The Queen works with Russia to stop it."
lines.junior: Lady Han says, "Japan wants more power in Korea. The Queen works with Russia to stop that."
lines.master: Lady Han explains, "Japan wants more power in Korea, and the Queen works with Russia to stop it."

lines.rookie: "Some men want to stop her."
lines.junior: "So some men want to stop her."
lines.master: "That is why some men want her stopped."

lines.rookie: The King folds the map slowly.
lines.junior: Slowly, the King folds the map.
lines.master: The King folds the map slowly, saying nothing.

lines.rookie: Now I know they are watching me.
lines.junior: Now I know that they are watching me.
lines.master: So now I know I am being watched.
